newsitem.title: PERU: Chronology of Peru's two-month hostage crisis.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of Peru's two-month hostage crisis.

text.p: Peru's Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels still hold 72 hostages after storming the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima two months ago.
Here is a chronology of the main events:

TUESDAY, Dec. 17 - About 15 heavily armed rebels swarm into the residence during a reception and capture hundreds of guests including government officials and foreign diplomats. They free all 80 women and some elderly men soon after the attack.
WEDNESDAY, Dec. 18 - The rebels threaten to kill their hostages unless the government frees up to 500 jailed comrades.
THURSDAY, Dec. 19 - Four ambassadors are released to be a "communications channel" between the rebels and the government.
FRIDAY, Dec. 20 - Rebels free 38 hostages.
SATURDAY, Dec. 21 - President Alberto Fujimori says he will study a non-violent "way out" if the rebels lay down their arms and free all hostages.
SUNDAY, Dec. 22 - Rebels free 225 hostages not linked to the government.
TUESDAY, Dec. 24 - Rebels release Uruguay's ambassador after his country frees two MRTA prisoners.
WEDNESDAY, Dec. 25 - A Japanese diplomat is released for medical reasons.
THURSDAY, Dec. 26 - An explosion is heard at the residence. Later the Guatemalan ambassador is freed.
SATURDAY, Dec. 28 - Government negotiator Domingo Palermo enters the residence for face-to-face negotiations with the MRTA. The rebels release 20 hostages.
TUESDAY, Dec. 31 - Cameramen enter building and interview rebel leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini. Later, the Honduran ambassador and an Argentine diplomat are freed.
WEDNESDAY, Jan. 1 - Rebels release seven captives, lowering hostage total to 74.

SUNDAY, Jan. 12 - Planned Palermo-Cerpa meeting is scrapped as rebels insist the talks centre on freedom for jailed MRTA members. Palermo proposes a guarantors commission of the government, MRTA, Red Cross and Vatican representative, Roman Catholic bishop Juan Luis Cipriani.
WEDNESDAY, Jan. 15 - Rebels accept idea of guarantors panel and suggest adding Guatemala and a European country.
THURSDAY, Jan. 16 - Government rejects Guatemala as guarantor and bans MRTA family visits organised by Red Cross.
FRIDAY, Jan. 17 - Rebels free an anti-terrorist police chief on medical grounds. Government and rebels agree on Canadian ambassador as member of the guarantor commission.
THURSDAY, Jan. 23 - Fujimori visits Bolivia and vows to wipe out MRTA rebels in the region after crisis.
FRIDAY, Jan. 24 - Police armoured cars rumble past the occupied residence.
SUNDAY, Jan. 26 - Rebels free an ill police chief.
MONDAY, Jan. 27 - Rebels shoot at police making lewd gestures as they pass residence in armoured vehicles.
WEDNESDAY, Jan. 29 - Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and Fujimori agree to meet in Toronto to discuss crisis after Tokyo's criticism of police tactics.
SATURDAY, Feb. 1 - Fujimori and Hashimoto agree to push for direct talks with rebels and appoint Japan's ambassador to Mexico, Terusuke Tarada, as observer at such negotiations.
MONDAY, Feb. 3 - U.S. President Bill Clinton meets Fujimori in Washington and applauds his handling of the crisis.
TUESDAY, Feb. 4 - Rebels shoot into air to commemorate fallen comrades. Fujimori returns home and slams MRTA for celebrating "acts of blood".
THURSDAY, Feb. 6 - Guarantors meet with rebels at compound to jump-start direct talks with the government.
SUNDAY, Feb. 9 - Fujimori announces talks on Feb. 11 between Palermo and rebel No. 2 Rolly Rojas, alias "The Arab."
MONDAY, Feb. 10 - Cerpa confirms Tuesday's talks. Rebels explode grenade and fire shots in response to "provocations."
TUESDAY, Feb. 11 - Rojas and Palermo meet for four hours in house opposite residence and agree to more face-to-face talks.
WEDNESDAY, Feb. 12 - The United States hails the restart of talks but adds no concessions should be made to "terrorists".
FRIDAY, Feb. 14 - Second round of talks to swap proposed agendas for future negotiations, new talks set for Saturday.
SATURDAY, Feb. 15 - Third round of talks is held but yields no tangible results.
MONDAY, Feb. 17 - 62nd day of standoff, beating Latin America's previous longest hostage siege: 1980 61-day seizure of Dominican Embassy and 57 hostages in Bogota by M-19 rebels.

The 72 hostages include Japanese and Bolivian ambassadors, Fujimori's brother and brother-in-law, top Peruvian government and security officials and about two dozen Japanese diplomats and businessmen.
